      public static String getTHFtype(String v, Map<String,Set<String>> typeMap)

    • preCheckExpr

      private static int preCheckExpr(Expr e, int found)
      Single-pass pre-check: walks the Expr tree once and returns a bitmask of the three conditions checked at the top of exclude(Expr, KB, Writer).

      Replacing three separate recursive helpers with one traversal avoids redundant pointer-chasing through the Java heap for every formula. An early-exit guard short-circuits as soon as all three flags are set.

      Bit meanings: PC_STR_LITERAL, PC_TRUE_FALSE, PC_FORMULA_ARG.

    • exclude

      public static boolean exclude(Expr e, KB kb, Writer out) throws IOException
      Expr-based overload of exclude(Formula, KB, Writer).

      Walks the Expr tree directly — no toKifString() round-trip, no new Formula() allocation. Every check mirrors its counterpart in the string-based overload.

      Call sites should prefer this overload whenever a non-null Expr is already available (e.g. in oneTransExpr and in the top-level loop of transModalTHF for Formula formulas).

      Throws:
      IOException

    • exclude

      public static boolean exclude(Formula fa, KB kb, Writer out) throws IOException
      Fast-path overload for Formula formulas.

      Uses fa.getFormula().contains() for the three pre-checks (JVM-intrinsic / SIMD-backed string scans) instead of the recursive preCheckExpr(com.articulate.sigma.parsing.Expr, int) tree walk, then delegates to excludeExprBody(com.articulate.sigma.parsing.Expr.SExpr, com.articulate.sigma.KB, java.io.Writer) for the structural checks. Called from the main loops in transModalTHF so that preCheckExpr is not invoked for every one of the ~75 K formulas.

      Throws:
      IOException

    • excludeExprBody

      private static boolean excludeExprBody(Expr.SExpr se, KB kb, Writer out) throws IOException
      Shared structural body for both exclude(Expr, …) and exclude(FormulaAST, …).

      Called after the three pre-checks (StrLiteral / LOG_TRUE/FALSE / Formula-arg) have already passed. Recursion into child SExpr nodes uses this method directly, so preCheckExpr(com.articulate.sigma.parsing.Expr, int) is never re-run on already-verified subtrees (eliminates the O(n²) redundancy of calling exclude(Expr) recursively).

      Throws:
      IOException

    • collectNumbersFromExpr

      private static void collectNumbersFromExpr(Expr e, Set<String> numbers)
      Expr-tree equivalent of collectNumbersFromFormula(java.lang.String, java.util.Set<java.lang.String>). Walks the Expr tree directly — no new Formula() allocation, no string re-scanning. Expr.NumLiteral nodes are the only leaves that can contribute numeric literals; all other leaf types (Atom, Var, RowVar, StrLiteral) are skipped.

    • collectNumbers

      public static Set<String> collectNumbers(KB kb)
      Scan all KB formulas and return the set of every numeric literal that appears (e.g. "24", "0.0", "360.0"). These will be declared as thf(n__24_tp,type,(n__24 : $i)). so that hideNumbers=true translations are well-typed. Dots are normalised to underscores to match the output of translateWord (0.0 -> n__0_0).

      Uses the Expr tree directly for Formula instances (no string re-scanning), and falls back to the string path for plain Formula objects.

    • analyzeFormulaExpr

      private static void analyzeFormulaExpr(Expr e, KB kb, Formula topLevel)
      Expr-tree equivalent of
      invalid reference 
      #analyzeFormula(Formula, KB)
      .

      Walks the Expr tree directly — no new Formula() allocation, no string re-parsing. Adds topLevel to badUsageSymbols if the given SExpr (or any sub-SExpr) has an argument position where the declared signature expects a non-Formula type but the argument is itself a compound expression (Expr.SExpr) or a predicate term.

      Parameters:
      e - the Expr node to analyze (may be any Expr subtype)
      kb - knowledge base (used for signature look-up)
      topLevel - the Formula to add to badUsageSymbols on detection

    • oneTransExpr

      public static void oneTransExpr(KB kb, Formula fa, PrintWriter bw) throws IOException
      Expr-based equivalent of
      invalid reference 
      #oneTrans
      . Used when the formula is a Formula with a non-null expr field.

      Pipeline:

      1. Run Modals.processModalsExpr(com.articulate.sigma.parsing.Expr, com.articulate.sigma.KB) on the original expr for type-info only.
      2. Preprocess the original expr with FormulaPreprocessor.preProcessExpr(com.articulate.sigma.Formula, boolean, com.articulate.sigma.KB).
      3. Build the typeMap from domain/range restrictions plus world-var entries from step 1.
      4. For each preprocessed Expr, apply modal processing again and translate to THF via ExprToTHF.translate(com.articulate.sigma.parsing.Expr, boolean, java.util.Map<java.lang.String, java.util.Set<java.lang.String>>).
      Throws:
      IOException

    • hasFormulaDomainArgMismatch

      public static boolean hasFormulaDomainArgMismatch(Expr e, Map<String,Set<String>> typeMap, KB kb)
      Returns true when e contains a predicate application where a Formula-typed domain argument is bound to a plain variable that is NOT typed Formula in typeMap (i.e. would be quantified as $i).

      This happens after pred-var expansion: the row-variable @ARGS is split into fresh Expr.Var nodes (?ARGS1 ?ARGS2 ?ARGS3 …) with no type annotation. If the predicate substituted for ?REL declares Formula as the domain type at position k, the variable ?ARGSk would be emitted as $i — but the predicate's THF type signature expects $o (or w > $o in modal mode). The result is an ill-typed THF axiom rejected by LEO-III / Vampire HOL.

      Predicates affected: attitudeForFormula (domain 3 = Formula), conclusion (domain 2), consistent (domains 1,2), fears (domain 2), hopes (domain 2), and others.

    • oneTransNonModalExpr

      public static void oneTransNonModalExpr(KB kb, Formula fa, Writer bw) throws IOException
      Expr-based equivalent of
      invalid reference 
      #oneTransNonModal
      . Used when the formula is a Formula with a non-null expr field (plain/non-modal THF generation).

      Pipeline:

      1. Preprocess the expr with FormulaPreprocessor.preProcessExpr(com.articulate.sigma.Formula, boolean, com.articulate.sigma.KB).
      2. Build the typeMap from domain/range restrictions.
      3. For each preprocessed Expr, translate to THF (non-modal) via ExprToTHF.translateNonModal(com.articulate.sigma.parsing.Expr, boolean, java.util.Map<java.lang.String, java.util.Set<java.lang.String>>).
      Throws:
      IOException
